articles.title: La Liga President Tebas slams Real Madrid refereeing ‘conspiracy’ claims
articles.summary: Madrid boss Jose Mourinho accuses officials of bias after his side’s 2-1 derby defeat by Atletico Madrid.
articles.body:
La Liga President Javier Tebas has hit out at what he calls accusations of a refereeing “conspiracy” by Real Madrid after their derby loss to Atletico Madrid.

Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho brought two printed screenshots of what he said were red-card tackles committed by Atletico players to his post-match news conference after Sunday’s 2-1 defeat.

Tebas responded to a pro-Real article on social media with a lengthy riposte on Tuesday to allegations of a “conspiracy” against the 15-time European champions.

“Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime’s television, building the same old narrative – the permanent conspiracy,” said Tebas, who has often been at odds with Real Madrid and the club’s outspoken president, Florentino Perez.

“This article goes further. It claims that referees harm ‘the business that feeds them’.

“What exactly is it asking for? Refereeing based on revenue, viewership or the badge? What a way to understand equality in the competition.

“Real Madrid are crucial to La Liga. But claiming that ‘La Liga is worth nothing’ without them reveals the disdain for the other clubs, their fans and their history. The competition belongs to no one.”

Madrid have made a stuttering start to the season and already sit six points behind reigning champions and early leaders Barcelona in the La Liga table.

“Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy,” Tebas added.

“That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.

“It’s more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what’s happening on the pitch.”

Real responded with ⁠a statement on their website condemning Tebas’s declarations and saying ⁠La Liga needs new leadership.

“Our club considers it intolerable that the president of La Liga uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking Real Madrid,” the statement said.

“Given this inappropriate and persistent behaviour, we believe that the ⁠professional football competition in Spain urgently needs a leader capable of managing it and realising its full potential with the fundamental ⁠duty of neutrality.”

Mourinho returned for a second spell in charge at the Santiago Bernabeu in the close season, tasked with ending a two-year spell without a major trophy.

After the heated capital derby on Sunday at Atletico’s Metropolitano Stadium, Mourinho was furious that Atletico defender Cristian Romero was not sent off for a stamp ⁠⁠on Jude Bellingham and also complained about a challenge by Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde before the visitors were themselves reduced to 10 men five minutes after half-time.

Valverde finished the match but was later diagnosed with “severe trauma to his left ankle”, the ⁠⁠club said in a statement. The midfielder will undergo further tests, it added.

“We could skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here,” Mourinho said, holding up the two images in what was the start of a near five-minute rant.

“Those were two clear red cards. The difficulties we’ve faced since the sending-off: 11 against 10. Well, we can imagine what 50 minutes of ‌‌11 against nine would have been like if justice had been done.”

articles.title: Mikel Arteta, Arsenal Reportedly Agree on New Contract, Latest Details on Extension
articles.summary: Arsenal and manager Mikel Arteta reportedly agreed to a new contract on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Arsenal and manager Mikel Arteta reportedly agreed to a new contract on Tuesday.

According to BBC's Sami Mokbel , the new deal includes a "sharp pay increase" from Arteta's current salary of £10 million per year plus £5 million in bonuses, and it is believed that the extension will keep him under contract until at least the 2029-30 season.

The 44-year-old Arteta's previous contract reportedly had been set to expire at the conclusion of the 2026-27 English Premier League campaign.

After playing in 110 matches for the Gunners from 2011 to 2016, Arteta spent time as an assistant coach at Manchester City, and he was then named Arsenal's manager in 2019.

Despite his lack of experience as a head man when he took the position, Arteta has enjoyed a great deal of success, especially as of late.

Arteta led Arsenal to the Premier League title last season, marking the club's first championship since 2004. On top of that, Arsenal were the 2025-26 UEFA Champions League runner-up.

Last season marked only the second time Arsenal ever reached the Champions League final, and although they fell to Paris Saint-Germain on penalty kicks, making it that far was another feather in Arteta's cap.

Finally winning the Champions League is a very plausible goal for Arsenal this season, as is winning back-to-back Premier League titles for the first time since winning three straight titles from 1933 to 1935 when it was known as the Football League First Division.

Arteta already has the Gunners off to a strong start in league play with four wins and one loss over their first five matches, placing them second in the table, three points behind undefeated Manchester City.

articles.title: Iván Fresneda, una locomotora para España
articles.standfirst: El lateral del Sporting de Portugal afronta su primera convocatoria con la selección absoluta.
articles.summary: El lateral del Sporting de Portugal afronta su primera convocatoria con la selección absoluta.
articles.body: Iván Fresneda celebrará su 22 cumpleaños el próximo lunes, durante la concentración de la selección española y a unas horas de medirse a Croacia en el Sánchez Pizjuán. Tenía la confianza de que la oportunidad podría llegar pronto, pero no tanto. La llamada de Luis de la Fuente se ha convertido en el mejor regalo posible y es el premio al trabajo duro de un joven futbolista que ha dado el salto definitivo a la élite en Portugal. "Es un sueño cumplido defender el escudo de país. Estoy con muchas ganas de devolver la confianza depositada en mí", explicó. Fresneda, que en la cantera del Real Madrid -donde estuvo hasta 2018- empezó jugando de delantero, pasó por el el Leganés y el Valladolid hasta llegar al Sporting Clube, donde es indiscutible en el lateral derecho. Con ellos debutó en Europa, brilló la temporada pasada en Champions y ha sido campeón de Liga y Copa en dos temporadas consecutivas, un hito que no se veía en el club desde hace más de 70 años. Una lesión el hombro no le puso fácil su primera temporada en Portugal, ya que estuvo varios meses fuera, pero volvió más fuerte y con la salida de Amorim y la llegada de Rui Borges su situación en el club dio un vuelco: ganó importancia, maduró, se consolidó y despertó el interés de varios clubes importantes. La temporada pasada jugó 39 partidos, marcó un gol y dio tres asistencias. Números que provocaron que este verano la Roma llegó a ofrecer 25 millones fijos y 5 en variables para incorporarlo, pero el Sporting no quiso vender. Su gran oportunidad en el fútbol profesional se la dio Pacheta cuando Iván era el lateral derecho del Juvenil A del Real Valladolid. Un jueves de noviembre, en un amistoso de entrenamiento contra el primer equipo, Iván brilló. Pacheta lo incorporó a los entrenamientos de forma habitual y en enero de 2022 debutó con el primer equipo en un partido de Copa del Rey ante el Real Betis. Tenía 17 años y se convirtió en el segundo jugador más joven de la historia en jugar con el primer equipo del Valladolid. El equipo acabó ascendiendo a Primera y la temporada siguiente Iván fue uno más de la plantilla guardando en su retina partidos brillantes como en el que logró amargarle la noche a Vinicius. Caprichos del destino, Fresneda ha seguido una trayectoria similar a la del jugador que sustituye en la absoluta: Pedro Porro, que también se marchó del Valladolid al Sporting, como Iván. "Lástima haber recibido esta oportunidad por la lesión de mi compañero y amigo Pedro Porro, al que le deseo que se recupere lo antes posible", declaró. Fresneda es un lateral profundo y de mucho recorrido. Una locomotora que la temporada pasada batió un récord de kilómetros recorridos en un partido durante el Sporting-Bodo Glimt, donde alcanzó los 17. Un jugador solidario en el esfuerzo en el campo y maduro fuera del mismo que habla castellano, inglés, portugués y un poco de alemán. Se matriculó en gestión deportiva, pero circunstancias personales y deportivas no le permitieron seguir la carrera con la regularidad que exige. Pese a ello, sigue formándose para asegurarse un futuro después del fútbol y mantiene la humildad que se necesita para triunfar dentro y fuera de los terrenos de juego.

articles.title: Luke Littler: Mark Webster says 'The Nuke' won't walk away from darts over booing and says PDC are trying to stop fans whistling
articles.summary: Sky Sports' Mark Webster believes Luke Littler will not walk away from darts over crowd treatment; Littler has won six majors this year including World Championship but World Series of Darts eluded him; watch Littler's World Grand Prix defence live on Sky Sports from September 28
articles.body:
Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was ended on Sunday after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, but the main talking point coming out of the event was Littler's continued fractious relationship with darts fans.

Indeed, earlier in the tournament Littler threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during victory over Nathan Aspinall.

The back-to-back world champion also faced a hostile environment during Friday's win over home favourite Danny Noppert and it escalated on Saturday night as referee Charlie Corstorphine had to intervene in the last-16 win over Aspinall.

Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there, but Webster does not believe Littler will leave the sport entirely over it.

"No, I don't think he's [Littler] going to walk away from the sport over this," Sky Sports Darts' Webster said.

"He was obviously very upset about how he was treated in the Netherlands at the weekend, but some of the opponents he played - a home favourite in Danny Noppert - he was going to get some rough treatment there.

"I'm not saying it's right, and the whistling, I know they're trying to take it out of the game.

"The booing, they won't be able to stop, but the whistling is something that's a bugbear to a lot of players at the minute. The PDC are trying to get rid of it.

"I spoke to a few of the security guys who are experimenting with stuff within the crowd, but obviously it got on top of Luke Littler this weekend.

"He was saying after games he wasn't happy with the treatment he got. I don't like saying it, but a lot of the booing is part of the game now.

"He kind of has drawn attention to it by speaking about it.

"The whistling is annoying, and I think it's a bit sharper when the players are throwing and it puts them off. A constant boo, I think players can deal with. Luke has dealt with it in the past, and I'm sure he'll be okay.

"If he chooses to miss events in the Netherlands, that's his prerogative. There is a Premier League night there, which I think he'll play, but the European Tour, there's 15 events during the year. He doesn't really need to go to the Netherlands, so he can cherry-pick there.

"So if he does decide to boycott, he can still plan out his year, really.

"He's got a long time left in the sport. I don't think he'll leave the sport as early as people make out.

"He loves playing darts and he's brilliant at it, so I think he'll just bounce back. He'll get some more rough treatment and he'll try and deal with it the way he has done the majority of the time, and just win games and win tournaments. He was a little bit hurt at the weekend."

'Littler is the main draw in darts - he'll bounce back'

Webster added that Littler remains the main face of darts after the 19-year-old's incredible achievements over recent years.

"We're still in this boom on the back of what he [Littler] did," he said.

"There's other players, but he is the main draw. After that run to the World Championships final on debut, and he's backed up by winning back-to-back World Championships. People buy a ticket to watch him. They may boo him, they may whistle when he throws.

"He's the best player in the world, and we've got this sort of culture in our country where the best players receive a bit of rough treatment. They want them knocked off their perch.

"He gets fired up himself, and I'm sure he'll bounce back in the right way at the Grand Prix in Leicester.

"It's easy to forget he's 19 because he's been around since he was 16, and he's done a lot in those three years. We're already talking about sort of holding every major. As good as he is, that's always going to be difficult.

"I don't think he should be too hard on himself about the weekend, he was beaten by the better man in Jonny. He acknowledged that. He was just a bit disappointed with the crowd.

"I fully expect him to win a few of the majors remaining. I think the European Championships will be a massive priority for him, because then he's ticked every box.

"And then obviously go on to Ally Pally and try and retain that, keep the streak going, and just keep cementing his place at world No 1.

"He's going to come away with some more major titles, that's for sure. I think these tournaments kind of favour him in terms of longer formats.

"Who's going to compete in there? It's going to be tough, but it's up to the other players and to see where his hunger is at in a minute."

Littler can still sweep the ranking events in 2026 - the World Series Finals, like the World Cup and Premier League, is non-ranked - if he wins the remaining four majors in Leicester, Dortmund, Wolverhampton and Minehead this autumn.

'The Nuke' has withdrawn from two Players Championship events in the Netherlands less than 24 hours after his bid for a PDC majors title clean sweep was dashed.

The teenager - currently £16,750 adrift of the final qualification spot - had hinted he may not try to reach the Players Championship Finals should his hopes of a major sweep end in the Netherlands.

Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the World Grand Prix (September 28-October 4), Grand Slam of Darts (November 14-22) and World Darts Championship (December 10-January 3) all live. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

articles.title: Revolución 'mundial' en los banquillos
articles.standfirst: Casi una veintena de selecciones nacionales han cambiado de entrenador tras la cita mundialista de Estado Unidos, México y Canadá
articles.summary: Casi una veintena de selecciones nacionales han cambiado de entrenador tras la cita mundialista de Estado Unidos, México y Canadá
articles.body: Un Mundial no termina cuando se entrega la Copa. Para muchas selecciones es precisamente entonces cuando empieza otro campeonato: el de reconstruir todo lo que no funcionó durante los cuatro años anteriores. Y el Mundial de 2026 ha dejado una revolución especialmente profunda en los banquillos. Múltiples han sido los técnicos que habían dirigido durante el torneo dejaron sus puestos durante la competición o inmediatamente después, aproximadamente un tercio de los entrenadores presentes en la cita. Algunos fueron víctimas directas del resultado, otros asumieron personalmente el fracaso, hubo contratos diseñados para terminar con el Mundial y también despedidas planificadas con muchos meses de antelación, como la de Didier Deschamps en Francia. No todos, por tanto, fueron despedidos. El Mundial funcionó más bien como una gigantesca frontera entre ciclos. Y lo que viene ahora es igualmente importante: Eurocopa 2028, Copa América, Copa de África, Copa Asiática y, en el horizonte, el Mundial de 2030. Sabri Lamouchi fue la primera víctima y ni siquiera llegó al final del Mundial. Túnez lo destituyó inmediatamente después de la goleada por 5-1 de su estreno. Fue una decisión extrema: apenas llevaba unos meses en el puesto. La Federación recurrió a Hervé Renard durante el propio campeonato, pero el cambio tampoco consiguió transformar el rumbo tunecino y Renard terminó igualmente su etapa, que ahora es el seleccionador de Costa de Marfil. En la actual, Túnez está dirigida por Mouin Chaabani. Mucho más doloroso fue el caso de Marcelo Bielsa. Uruguay llegaba al campeonato con unas expectativas muy superiores a lo que finalmente ofreció: dos empates y una derrota ante España dejaron a la Celeste fuera en la primera fase. El propio Bielsa había llegado al Mundial con un contrato que terminaba con el torneo y asumió públicamente la responsabilidad. "No puedo justificar la posición en la que terminamos", reconoció el argentino, que consideró insuficiente la gestión que había realizado de los recursos a su disposición. Su salida fue, por tanto, una mezcla de final de contrato y renuncia tras el resultado deportivo, no una destitución convencional. El objetivo, por tanto, no es otro que regenerar el proyecto sin desmontar una generación de enorme calidad y volver a convertir a Uruguay, ya con Diego Forlán al frente, en aspirante real a la Copa América y al Mundial 2030. Steve Clarke también dio un paso al lado después de que Escocia no consiguiera superar la fase de grupos. Fue una salida voluntaria provocada por la sensación de haber alcanzado el final de un ciclo. Sebastien Pocognoli tendrá la misión de mantener la capacidad de Escocia para clasificarse regularmente para las grandes competiciones, pero dar el salto de competir a superar rondas. La eliminación mundialista también acabó con la etapa de Miroslav Koubek. El veterano entrenador checo renunció después de que su selección no consiguiera atravesar la primera fase. Reconstruir alrededor de la nueva generación y volver a colocar a Chequia de manera estable en Mundiales y Eurocopas. Ese es el objetivo del español Santi Denia. Hong Myung-bo tampoco sobrevivió a la primera ronda. El seleccionador surcoreano dejó el puesto tras un Mundial decepcionante y una eliminación prematura. Con la llegada del español Robert Moreno, se tratará de mantener la hegemonía clasificatoria en Asia, renovar una plantilla que necesita mirar más allá de su generación de figuras veteranas y preparar el ciclo de 2030. Si las salidas anteriores podían entrar de alguna manera dentro de la lógica del torneo, Alemania fue el terremoto. Alemania había ganado su grupo, pero cayó ante Paraguay por penaltis en dieciseisavos. Julian Nagelsmann decidió dejar el cargo después de reflexionar sobre una eliminación que la Federación y el propio entrenador consideraron incompatible con las aspiraciones de la Mannschaft. "Después de una decepción tan amarga, merecen la oportunidad de empezar de nuevo", señaló Nagelsmann al comunicar su decisión. La DFB se decantó por Jürgen Klopp como sucesor. Y con él se prevé una amplia reconstrucción del rodillo alemán. La selección neerlandesa también cambió su banquillo después de caer en las eliminatorias. Ronald Koeman dejó el puesto tras la eliminación, poniendo fin a otro proyecto que aspiraba a mucho más. Ahora, con Xavi Hernández al frente, habrá que transformar una selección con calidad suficiente para estar entre las mejores de Europa en una candidata efectiva a los títulos. En Países Bajos, el listón vuelve a estar en la Euro 2028 y el Mundial 2030. Sebastián Beccacece cerró su etapa después de que Ecuador no alcanzara los objetivos marcados en Norteamérica. Su salida formó parte del grupo de técnicos que dejaron sus selecciones al quedar fuera de las primeras eliminatorias. El objetivo de Marcelo Gallardo será aprovechar una de las generaciones más interesantes del fútbol ecuatoriano y consolidarse ya no sólo como mundialista, sino como equipo capaz de disputar las rondas decisivas. El caso de Zlatko Dalic es diferente. Después de una trayectoria extraordinaria con Croacia, su contrato terminó con el Mundial y la Federación decidió no prolongarlo. Su marcha fue presentada como una despedida a una etapa histórica, no como un despido traumático. Slaven Bilić, como nuevo seleccionador, deberá acometer la transición generacional más delicada de Croacia en muchos años y demostrar que los éxitos de la era Dalic no dependían exclusivamente de la generación de Luka Modric. Aquí sí hubo bisturí. Pape Thiaw fue destituido después de la eliminación de Senegal contra Bélgica. La Federación decidió cortar el proceso y empezar nuevamente. Para ello, y con el fin de volver a dominar África, Senegal ha puesto al equipo en manos de Patrick Vieira, quien considera que su plantilla está preparada para pelear por las Copas de África y convertirse de forma permanente en una selección capaz de avanzar rondas en los Mundiales. La situación de Carlos Queiroz también requiere matices. El portugués había llegado a Ghana con un acuerdo de corta duración ligado a la participación mundialista. Tras caer ante Colombia, se despidió públicamente y el vínculo llegó a su final. Sin embargo, todo se recondujo y las partes volvieron a encontrarse y a comienzos de este mes confirmaron el regreso del luso al banquillo ghanés, al menos, en la próxima Copa Africana de Naciones de 2027. El caso mexicano es probablemente el más limpio de todos. Javier Aguirre sabía antes del Mundial que su aventura terminaba allí. La Federación había preparado la sucesión para que Rafa Márquez, integrante de su cuerpo técnico, asumiera el siguiente ciclo. Así, Márquez recibe una selección que aspira a aprovechar el trabajo desarrollado para conseguir de una vez el salto competitivo que México lleva décadas buscando en las eliminatorias mundialistas. Otro de los grandes nombres de la lista es Roberto Martínez. Portugal cayó 1-0 contra España en octavos y el seleccionador español entendió que había llegado el momento de parar. "Es el fin de un ciclo", explicó Martínez, que añadió una frase todavía más contundente: había llegado a Portugal "para ganar el Mundial" y, sin conseguirlo, entendía que no tenía sentido continuar. No fue formalmente un despido, sino final de contrato y decisión de no continuar, con la llegada además de un nuevo presidente federativo, Pedro Proença, al que Martínez consideraba legitimado para elegir su propio seleccionador: en este caso a Jorge Jesús, que inicia quien sabe si el proyecto post Cristiano Ronaldo, o al menos preparar esa transición, manteniendo al equipo como aspirante inmediato a la Euro 2028 y al Mundial 2030. El caso de Rudi García demuestra que no todas las salidas responden al fracaso. Bélgica llegó hasta cuartos de final y fue eliminada por España, posteriormente campeona, pero García y la Federación decidieron de común acuerdo no ampliar el contrato que expiraba el 31 de julio. "Dejo a Bélgica en la Liga A de la Nations League y entre los ocho mejores equipos del mundo", recordó al despedirse. La propia Federación destacó que había recuperado la cohesión de los Diablos Rojos y ayudado a gestionar la transición de su generación dorada, de la que ya se está encargando Mark van Bommel. La marcha de Didier Deschamps no tuvo nada que ver con el resultado del Mundial. En enero de 2025 ya había anunciado públicamente que 2026 significaría su final como seleccionador. "He cumplido mi tiempo", explicó entonces. Terminó así una etapa iniciada en 2012 que dejó, entre otros éxitos, el Mundial de 2018, la final de 2022, la Nations League de 2021 y otra presencia entre los cuatro mejores en 2026. Zidane tiene ante sí el único objetivo posible para Francia: ganar cada torneo que disputa, empezando por la Euro 2028 y culminando en el Mundial 2030. Hay que añadir una última salida posterior que permite dimensionar todavía mejor la inestabilidad post Mundial: Hugo Broos dejó oficialmente Sudáfrica el 31 de julio, cuando concluyó su contrato. Y aquí tampoco hubo castigo deportivo. Todo lo contrario. Sudáfrica había regresado a un Mundial y conseguido superar por primera vez la primera fase. Broos explicó que las largas ausencias lejos de su familia y los momentos de soledad en Sudáfrica eran el motivo de su decisión de no renovar. Su trayectoria había incluido además el tercer puesto en la Copa de África y la recuperación de una selección que llevaba años lejos del primer plano. Ahora, Pitso Mosimane se hace cargo del equipo. A todos estos movimientos, hay que sumar otros más en dos selecciones que no pasaron desapercibidas en el Mundial: Cabo Verde y Haití. En el primer caso, Bubista dio paso a la llegada de Humberto Bettencourt; en el segundo, Migné sale para que llegue David Badí. Máxima ilusión en ambos combinados.

articles.title: FIFA President Infantino’s letter a ploy for re-election, says German FA
articles.summary: Infantino proposed an independent review of FIFA’s decision-making process amid criticism of his leadership.
articles.body:
A letter from FIFA President Gianni Infantino this week to ⁠all 211 members, offering to discuss reforms within world football’s governing body – amid an ongoing crisis over his failed plan to sell a stake in the World Cup – is a ⁠mere ploy to get himself re-elected, Germany’s Football Association (DFB) President Bernd Neuendorf has said.

In Monday’s letter seen by the Reuters news agency, Infantino proposed an independent review of FIFA’s decision-making process, in a move that could help him regain support after the withdrawal of his controversial private investment plan.

Striking a ‌conciliatory tone, he also said he would propose consultations with confederations, member associations and other stakeholders about strengthening FIFA’s decision-making.

Infantino faced a fierce backlash over his proposal to sell a 20 percent stake in FIFA’s commercial rights, including the World Cup, to private investors.

The plan was abandoned in July after strong opposition and boycott threats, with UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF calling for changes to FIFA’s leadership.

They said there had been no consultation with any continental confederation at ⁠any stage, with Infantino acting alone. UEFA has said a change in leadership was now necessary, with the European body having lost faith in the current president.

“I regard Gianni Infantino’s letter as a transparent ploy to secure ⁠his re-election next year,” said DFB President Neuendorf on Tuesday. “Fundamentally, FIFA now seems to have recognised that changes are essential.

“However, Gianni Infantino ⁠is definitely not the right person to lead a reform ⁠process. He has squandered all credibility.”

Neuendorf is also a member of the FIFA Council, the organisation’s main decision-making body.

Infantino said in the letter that member associations’ positions on proposals or governance matters would not affect their ‌treatment by FIFA, whose development and solidarity programmes would continue under existing rules.

The Swiss is up for re-election in March next year, with his opponents struggling to find a candidate ‌to ‌challenge the president. Sources familiar with the discussions told Reuters this month that he still had enough votes to win, prompting opponents to focus on curbing his powers.

articles.title: Almeida: "Casablanca tiene más opciones que Madrid para ser la sede de la final del Mundial 2030"
articles.standfirst: El alcalde de Madrid participó en un desayuno informativo organizado por el Heraldo de Aragón
articles.summary: El alcalde de Madrid participó en un desayuno informativo organizado por el Heraldo de Aragón
articles.body: El alcalde de Madrid, José Luis Martínez Almeida, ha asegurado esta misma mañana que Casablanca tiene más opciones de acoger la final del Mundial 2030 que Madrid. Lo ha hecho tras criticar la gestión del Gobierno en Ceuta y asegurar que Marruecos sí está moviéndose para ser sede finalista. "No soy optimista porque considero, y esto es legítimo por parte de Marruecos y el Rey de Marruecos, que ellos quieren esa final y lógicamente ellos yo creo que están actuando a nivel político e institucional para lograr esa final", afirmó Almeida. "Lo que yo no tengo, es ninguna prueba, ni ninguna evidencia de que el Gobierno se esté moviendo en ese mismo sentido. Que la final no sea en Madrid tiene que hacerse replantear si el Mundial se tiene que celebrar o no, no soy quien tiene que decirlo, pero si la final no se celebra en Madrid creo que debería haber consecuencias", aseguró el alcalde de Madrid. La realidad es que la sede del final del Mundial 2030 se está convirtiendo en un 'tema de Estado'. Lo deportivo, de momento, está quedando en un segundo plano. Lo que debería ser una fiesta para el fútbol y un motivo de consenso entre países, que en su día decidieron organizar de forma conjunta el Mundial, ha tornado en una lucha cargada de connotaciones geopolíticas. De hecho, hace unas semanas, el presidente de la Federación Real Marroquí de Fútbol , Fouzi Lekjaa, afirmó que la final del Mundial 2030 se jugará en el Gran Estadio Hassan II de Casablanca, que aún está en construcción. "La provincia de Benslimán es la que tendrá el honor de organizar la final del Mundial de 2030. El que quiera estar en el próximo gobierno no tiene otra opción que desarrollar la provincia", aseguró en plena batalla electoral por la presidencia. El Gran Estadio Hassan II, cuya inauguración está prevista para finales de 2027, es un recinto de 115.000 plazas que está llamado a ser el mayor del mundo por capacidad, y con el que Marruecos compite con el Santiago Bernabéu de Madrid para acoger la final del Mundial de 2030.

articles.title: ‘Every player wants to win it’: Kylian Mbappé eyes first Ballon d’Or award
articles.summary: Soccer superstar Kylian Mbappé says there is no “frustration” over not yet winning a Ballon d’Or – an annual award given to the world’s best player – but tells CNN Sports that this “could be a good year for me.”
articles.body: Soccer superstar Kylian Mbappé says there is no “frustration” over not yet winning a Ballon d’Or – an annual award given to the world’s best player – but tells CNN Sports that this “could be a good year for me.” Mbappé did not win any silverware last season – often a huge factor in the decision-making process – finishing fourth at the World Cup with France and failing to win a trophy with Real Madrid. But speaking to CNN Sports amid a new sponsorship deal with sportswear brand On, he says he still has a chance of winning, arguing that the award should be given to the best individual player. “Football is a collective sport, but there are collective trophies to represent that collective supremacy,” he tells CNN Sports. “When you talk about the Ballon d’Or, you give it to one player, so you give it to the best player, and the guy who shows you that he is the best, and every big competition shows something.” Mbappé’s two biggest contenders for this year appear to be Barcelona wonderkid Lamine Yamal and Bayern Munich star Harry Kane. There is also support for Lionel Messi to win it for a record-extending ninth time, mainly due to his performances for Argentina at the World Cup. And although falling just short of winning a second World Cup trophy with France, Mbappé also had a tournament to remember. The 27-year-old became the World Cup’s all-time top scorer, netting a record-breaking 22nd goal during the third-place playoff against England. “It’s something that I couldn’t imagine,” he says about the achievement. “We saw all the greatest players of all time, all the greatest athletes, all the greatest icons that I idolized when I was younger, and to be able to be this guy at only 27, it sounds surreal. “At the end of the day, it’s part of history, part of the legacy that I want to build.” It’s just one of the many records Mbappé has broken during his illustrious career that makes it even more surprising that his name has never been written into the Ballon d’Or history books. “A frustration? No,” he tells CNN Sports about never having won it. “Because, as a competitor, you always want to win everything. So at the end of the day, of course you want to win it, every player wants to win it, but we have to wait.” New era for France But regardless of who wins the award at the ceremony in London on October 26, this will still be a big year for the striker – especially with the national team. Legendary France boss Didier Deschamps stepped down from his role following the World Cup, meaning Mbappé will have to get used to a new national team coach for the first time. Replacing Deschamps is none other than Zinedine Zidane, arguably the greatest player to ever suit up for Les Bleus. Zidane – who oversaw a dynasty at Real Madrid, winning three consecutive Champions League titles, but who is taking charge of an international team for the first time – has already confirmed Mbappé will be his captain as the country looks to start a new cycle ahead of the next men’s World Cup in 2030. “Another era starting in the national team, we are really happy to have him (Zidane). Let’s see what we’re gonna do. I think everybody expects a lot from us,” Mbappé says, adding that there are plenty of lessons to learn from the team’s performance in North America this summer. “We are one of the best teams in the world, everybody saw. But we have to work on the details to be the best in the world, and I think also everybody saw that. “At the end of the day, it was an amazing experience for us because I think we gave pleasure to fans all around the world, but we didn’t achieve what we wanted to achieve. But I cannot say it’s a failure.” Signing for On It’s not just a new era starting with the national team, though. Mbappé has also ended a near 20-year relationship with Nike to sign with On – marking the sportswear brand’s first step into the world of soccer. The Swiss-based company announced this month that Mbappé will become a global ambassador and “work directly with On’s product teams” on footwear and apparel, including On’s Lightspray technology that makes shoes with the help of robots. “It’s a new chapter, a new challenge, a new opportunity, and I’m really happy about the situation right now,” Mbappé says. “I think it’s also part of a moment in my life that I wanted to change, an evolution as a person, as a player … but as a person also, I wanted something different. I wanted it to be at the start of a journey to build a legacy, completely build the legacy and it was the perfect opportunity for me.” The Frenchman has been heavily involved in developing the “perfect boot” and says he wants it to feel like a “second skin.” But when can fans expect to see Mbappé in his new design? “We do our market entry in 2027, and before that, I don’t know. We continue with the last prototyping, so we might get a glimpse at some point,” On-Founder and Co-CEO David Allemann tells CNN Sports. “For us, this is an opportunity to bring in innovation. Kylian spoke about it: It’s about the details. So it’s about how you can spray a shoe in three minutes with a robotic arm that can influence every pixel on that boot, reinforce it where it needs reinforcement, bring flexibility where it needs it, and pretty much build a second skin for your foot, bringing the shortest distance between your foot and the ball. We see it as an opportunity.”

articles.title: Fifa reform claims questioned by FAW chief Noel Mooney
articles.summary: Football Association of Wales chief executive Noel Mooney challenges suggestions Fifa is planning major reforms.
articles.body:
Football Association of Wales chief executive Noel Mooney has played down suggestions Fifa is planning major reforms.

Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of how world football's governing body operates and says he is open to reform.

In a letter sent to members of the Fifa Council and all of its national associations, Infantino explains the independent process would "recommend potential improvements".

"I've seen the headlines today about major reform at Fifa - that's not how the letter read to me, to be frank," Mooney said.

"I saw the letter itself that was sent out, it doesn't actually say reform of Fifa itself.

"It talks about reform around strategic projects and initiatives.

"They would look at how they were consulted and how decisions were made around that."

Infantino says he is open to talks over Fifa reform

FAW chief calls for Infantino to step down

Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

That would have involved selling stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, and it sparked a major backlash.

The Welsh governing body was among the first national associations to withdraw backing for Infantino's bid to continue his leadership of Fifa.

Infantino will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

Mooney reiterated the FAW would not be endorsing Infantino's candidature.

"With the Fifa president, you're looking for a moral guardian of the game," Mooney told the BBC Radio Wales Phone In.

"You're not looking for somebody to sell off parts of the game.

"The World Cup does not need private equity. They have billions and billions of dollars in reserve.

"Give us the money. Let us build the pitches. You've got loads of reserves. Let's have it as soon as possible.

"There was a summit in Miami before as the World Cup kicked off, a meeting of all 211 federations.

"I stood up at that meeting and said, look, I mean, the revenue for Qatar was around eight billion.

"The revenue for this World Cup in Canada, USA and Mexico is 16 billion. Therefore, it's 100% increase in revenue, give us 100% growth."

articles.title: El Barcelona vuelve a empezar
articles.standfirst: El vigente campeón de la Champions League regresa a la competición midiéndose al Paris FC en el Johan Cruyff
articles.summary: El vigente campeón de la Champions League regresa a la competición midiéndose al Paris FC en el Johan Cruyff
articles.body: Han pasado 123 días desde que el Barcelona conquistara su cuarta Champions League tras derrotar al OL Lyonnes en Oslo. Las azulgrana regresan a la máxima competición continental dando el pistoletazo de salida a la fase Liga midiéndose este miércoles (21:00 horas) al Paris FC en el estadio Johan Cruyff. "Tengo un gran recuerdo de Oslo, pero ya pasó y queda atrás", subrayó Pere Romeu, técnico culé. "Tenemos un nuevo reto. De momento no hemos hecho nada. Comenzamos de nuevo", añadió. Cuatro meses desde la gesta en el Ullevaal Stadion que han dado para mucho movimiento en la plantilla azulgrana, hoy sin Alexia Putellas, Mapi León, Ona Batlle, Salma Paralluelo, Txell Font, Giulia Dragoni ni Martine Fenger y con Kerolin Nicoli, Martina Fernández, Renee van Asten y Tyler McCamey. "Seguimos siendo un muy buen equipo, una referencia, con una identidad muy marcada y con jugadoras de mucho nivel, si no las mejores", expuso Romeu, que sabe que todos los focos apuntan a su equipo. "Hasta ahora no sé si hemos sido favoritas o no, pero lo que hemos hecho es prepararnos para ganar y esta temporada lo volveremos a hacer", relató. "Si estás en este equipo, optas por todo. Esto es lo primero. Seas joven, seas veterana, lleves más años en el club o acabes de llegar", subrayó. El Barcelona regresa a la casilla de salida con la intención de revalidar el póker logrado el año pasado y sumar la Copa de Campeonas a su palmarés. "Cada temporada es una nueva oportunidad. Por un tema numérico y obvio, hubo jugadoras la temporada pasada que seguramente no tuvieron la oportunidad de jugar grandísimos partidos, pese a ser muy, muy buenas, y seguramente esta temporada se les abrirá ese escenario", explicó. "Estamos en un momento, individualmente hablando, en el que hay jugadoras que están demostrando un nivel individual altísimo para estar en septiembre. Y eso habla muy bien del día a día, de nuestro entrenamiento y del nivel colectivo", aseveró. En el plano deportivo, todo apunta a que Romeu no podrá contar con Vicky López ni Kika Nazareth, ausentes en el último entrenamiento previo al choque. El primer rival europeo del curso será el Paris FC, subcampeón de la Liga francesa entrenado por Sandrine Soubeyrand. "Nuestro objetivo es llegar a Polonia, a Varsovia, pero el camino es muy largo. Hay muchos partidos y tenemos que ir partido a partido, paso a paso", aseguró Ewa Pajor, ariete polaca del Barcelona. "Cuando eres el mejor equipo del mundo, los otros equipos quieren jugar muy bien contra ti. Para ellos es una motivación, pero nosotras estamos preparadas", dijo. La que fuera máxima goleadora de la UWCL la temporada pasada también habló de su futuro, dado que su contrato con el Barcelona caduca a final de temporada. "Quiero jugar en el Barça muchos más años porque es el club en el que puedo mejorar cada día, porque hay mucha calidad en el equipo y en el staff, porque son personas que nos hacen mejorar cada día como equipo", sentenció.

articles.title: Erling Haaland Trolls Manchester United Fan Over Viral 'No Haircut Challenge' in Social Media Post
articles.summary: Erling Haaland got in a dig at noted Manchester United fan Frank Ilett over his "no haircut challenge" that dates back to 2024.
articles.body:
Erling Haaland got in a dig at noted Manchester United fan Frank Ilett over his "no haircut challenge" that dates back to 2024.

Afer Ilett, better known as The United Strand, commented on a post suggesting Haaland's recent haircut was a dig at United, the Manchester City star clapped back by telling him to "cut your hair man."

In October 2024, Ilett vowed not to cut his hair until Manchester United won five straight games. He recently posted a video on Instagram showing how his hair looks after 712 days of not getting it cut because the Red Devils have yet to reach the goal he set.

Haaland debuted a fresh haircut on Aug. 23, the same day City kicked off the Premier League season. The Blues have won their first five matches of the season, including a 1-0 victory over United on Sept. 13.

Manchester City currently sits atop the Premier League table as the lone undefeated club remaining after five weeks. United is 12th in the standings with a 1-2-2 record coming off a draw against Fulham on Sunday.

articles.standfirst: Será el nuevo entrenador del equipo Sub19
articles.summary: Será el nuevo entrenador del equipo Sub19
articles.body: De Italia... a Grecia. Olympiacos ha anunciado que el joven entrenador español David Rodríguez asumirá el cargo de entrenador del equipo sub-19. El vallisoletano cambia Italia por Grecia después de sus etapas como asistente en el Modena de Serie B, entrenador del equipo Primavera o segundo técnico de Ignazio Abate en el Milan Primavera. El joven técnico español de 34 años también había trabajado anteriormente en el CD Parquesol, CD Villa de Simancas, CD San Agustín, Real Valladolid, Betis CF, CD Pedroñeras y CD Alcorcón. David Rodríguez se incorpora, por lo tanto, a la exigente academia de un Olympiacos que toma un nuevo rumbo con la llegada de Antonio Cordón a la Dirección Deportiva. Tras la salida de Mendilibar, semanas atrás, Imanol Alguacil asumió el mando del primer equipo.

articles.title: Los árbitros piden a los entrenadores “respeto y empatía”
articles.standfirst: El presidente del CTA, Fran Soto, contundente ante las polémicas palabras de Mourinho (que fue el gran ausente de la cita) tras el derbi como desveló en exclusiva Radio MARCA
articles.summary: El presidente del CTA, Fran Soto. contundente ante las polémicas palabras de Mourinho (que fue el gran ausente de la cita) tras el derbi como desveló en exclusiva Radio MARCA
articles.body: La reunión del Comité de Entrenadores ha centrado la actualidad esta mañana en la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas, más si cabe tras la polémica que todavía colea después del derbi madrileño entre Atlético de Madrid y Real Madrid. En la asamblea de dicho colectivo, Fran Soto, presente en calidad de presidente del CTA, ha insistido en la importancia del respeto a la figura arbitral, pidiendo a los entrenadores “empatía como responsables de sus equipos” con el objetivo de seguir humanizando la figura del colegiado. A la reunión han acudido un buen número de entrenadores de Primera división, caso de Hansi Flick (se marchó rápidamente para estar presente en el entrenamiento vespertino de su equipo), Diego Pablo Simeone o Edin Terzic, así como representantes de Segunda u otros que ahora no tienen banquillo como Éder Sarabia o Marcelino García Toral. Entre las ausencias más sonadas, Manuel Pellegrini y especialmente, José Mourinho. Tampoco estuvo José Bordalás. Para el colectivo arbitral: “nosotros solo podemos empatar o perder”. Por ahí, esa insistencia en la comprensión y el respeto hacia su figura tras todo lo acontecido en el último derbi, en el que Mourinho señaló de manera clara y directa al colegiado Ortiz Arias. Pese a que el preparador del Real Madrid no ha estado presente, sus palabras tras el derbi aún resuenan. De hecho, hay mensajes, como el del jefe de gabinete de La Liga, Víctor Martín Ortega, que ha incidido en “la misma importancia de los diez partidos de cada jornada y los diez arbitrajes de cada partido”, y que recuerdan al recadito, en forma de falta de experiencia internacional, dirigido por Mou a Ortiz Arias. Antes de esa charla, los asistentes recibieron una sesión de coaching a cargo de Xesco Espar, mítico entrenador de balonmano en el Barcelona. Además, se confirmó que tanto la jugada de Kang In Lee con Valverde como el lance entre Cuti Romero y Bellingham serán analizadas en Tiempo de revisión.

articles.title: Scotland: Sebastien Pocognoli has 'good mix' as new head coach targets winning start in Nations League
articles.summary: The new head coach takes charge for the first time against Slovenia in the Nations League on Saturday; Scotland are also away to N. Macedonia with games against Switzerland and Slovenia at Hampden during this international break; six newcomers are included in the Belgian's first squad
articles.body:
The Belgian is meeting his players for the first time this week as they train in the La Manga sunshine ahead of their Nations League opener against Slovenia.

Five players were handed their maiden full Scotland call-ups in his initial squad, with Blackburn Rovers midfielder Kristi Montgomery drafted in following the withdrawals of Kieran Tierney and Kenny McLean.

The longer international break - with four Nations League matches - gives the new boss more time with his squad as he looks to make an impact as Steve Clarke's successor.

"We have plenty of experience in the team, there are some new faces and young lads, and I think we have a good mix," Pocognoli told Sky Sports News.

"We need to make sure that the balance stays right, and to keep what makes the Scotland team really strong, it was the cohesion and really proper DNA in the team, and this needs to stay.

"The needed change was at this moment, because we follow the timelines, and the change is just about the things that we want to create on the pitch.

"It's also performance in your club, injury, and at the same time you need to make the change.

"What was provided in the past is massive to use it for the future.

"It's to find the right balance, like I said, so the experienced players will be important to continue to take care of this, and on the coaching staff point of view, we need to be aligned about what we want to achieve together.

"I want to see a team who are just really together, it's quite basic, attack together, defend together, but that's part of the Scotland mentality."

The Pocognoli era officially gets underway in Ljubljana on Saturday, with a game against Switzerland at Hampden Park three days later.

The squad then fly to North Macedonia on October 3 before returning to Glasgow to face Slovenia again on October 6.

Scotland were demoted from Nations League A after a play-off defeat by Greece last year and return to the second tier for this year's competition.

"There are many ways to be successful," the 39-year-old added.

"For me, in the Nations League, it's to stay competitive and try to be as much as possible higher in the ranking to go to League A.

"But just to recognise some principles on the pitch, recognise who are the leaders on the pitch, see some young lads playing, see team cohesion on the pitch.

"Also, to get the supporters excited. If we can combine with the result, and that's why we do this job, I would be really happy."

Defenders: Luis Binks (Brondby), Josh Doig (Sassuolo), Colby Donovan (Celtic), Luke Graham (Stoke City), Jack Hendry (Al-Ettifaq), Aaron Hickey (Brentford), Scott McKenna (Dinamo Zagreb), Nathan Patterson (Torino), Andy Robertson (Tottenham), Stephen Welsh (Swansea City)

articles.title: Irlanda jugará contra Israel pese las protestas: "No jugamos con el genocidio, jugamos contra el genocidio"
articles.standfirst: Más de 160 deportistas irlandeses piden a su selección que boicoteen el duelo
articles.summary: Más de 160 deportistas irlandeses piden a su selección que boicoteen el duelo
articles.body: Irlanda jugará contra Israel. Pese a la petición de boicot de sus propios compatriotas, la selección que dirige Heimir Hallgrimsson saltará al césped en Debrecen (Hungría) el próximo 27 de septiembre para medirse a uno de sus tres rivales de grupo (Austria y Kosovo lo completan). "Ninguno de nosotros se siente cómodo jugando, pero una vez que hemos decidido jugarlo, nos mantenemos unidos y jugamos como uno solo", dijo el islandés Heimir Hallgrimsson, seleccionador de Irlanda, que dejó una frase que ha sentado fatal en su rival: "No estamos jugando con un genocidio, estamos jugando contra un genocidio. Estamos jugando contra Israel, no estamos jugando con Israel". La federación de fútbol de Israel respondió con un comunicado en su cuenta de Twitter: "Hemos contribuido al mundo y a la humanidad en innumerables campos, ganando un impresionante número de Premios Nobel en el camino. Desafortunadamente, aún no hemos encontrado una cura para la estupidez, la ignorancia y la hipocresía exhibidas por el entrenador del equipo de Irlanda. No estamos jugando con la ignorancia, la hipocresía y la estupidez, estamos jugando contra el entrenador que las encarna". Irlanda es uno de los países más críticos con el genocidio en Gaza e, históricamente, uno de los más comprometidos con la causa palestina. Además del boicot a Eurovisión, que mantendrán por segundo año consecutivo, ya ha habido tensiones en otros deportes. En febrero de 2024, las selecciones femeninas de baloncesto de Irlanda e Israel se midieron en un duelo de clasificación para el Eurobasket de 2025. Las jugadoras irlandesas escucharon el himno de Israel junto a su banquillo y no en la pista enfrente de sus rivales, como suele hacerse. No hubo entrega de obsequios y las jugadoras tampoco se dieron la mano antes del salto inicial. En una carta firmada por más de 160 deportistas irlandeses, entre ellos olímpicos, exfutbolistas de la selección, exjugadores de rugby y boxeadores, señalan que la federación irlandesa de fútbol pudo haber tomado medidas antes, pero subrayan que aún se puede actuar para demostrar que el deporte está para unir a la gente. "No jugar este partido sería la cosa más deportiva que se podría hacer. Es un momento muy importante y es una oportunidad para hacer lo correcto. Ponerse la camiseta de Irlanda y representar a tu país significa mucho, pero la Irlanda que queremos representar es la que recuerda sus raíces anticolonialistas y resistencia antimperialista", destacan. "Este momento", añaden "simboliza algo muy profundo, mayor que el deporte. Pero esto también es deporte. Esto demostraría el verdadero poder del deporte para unir a la gente, recordar los valores que nos conectan a todos y mostrar el impacto más allá del partido".

articles.title: Nueve meses de 'Castrismo'
articles.standfirst: El entrenador portugués firmó por el Levante el pasado 20 de diciembre y acumula una media de 1.32 puntos por partidos
articles.summary: El entrenador portugués firmó por el Levante el pasado 20 de diciembre y acumula una media de 1.32 puntos por partidos
articles.body: Luís Castro cumple nueve meses como entrenador del Levante. El míster portugués aterrizó en el barrio de Orriols un 20 de diciembre y, desde entonces, ha dirigido un total de 28 encuentros oficiales, todos ellos de Primera División. Inmerso en una situación delicada, el técnico luso cogió las riendas del equipo después de un empate a uno ante la Real Sociedad, dirigido por los interinos Álvaro del Moral y Vicente Iborra, y situados en última posición con 10 puntos, a seis de la salvación, que en aquel momento la marcaba el Valencia. A partir de ahí, el cuadro azulgrana empezó a sumar puntos, hasta un total de 42 unidades, 32 desde que Castro cogió las riendas del equipo, para alcanzar la tan ansiada permanencia en la máxima categoría del fútbol español en la última jornada del campeonato en el estadio de la Cartuja ante el Real Betis. Esta temporada, con las seis jornadas que lleva disputadas de calendario el equipo valenciano, ha sumado un total de cinco puntos, con una victoria, ante el Real Betis, y dos empates, ante Osasuna y Málaga. En el total de envites dirigidos, Luís Castro lleva acumulado 28 encuentros, en los que ha conseguido diez victorias, siete empates y un total de once derrotas. Con estos números, suman una media de 1.32 puntos por partido, 0.25 menos de la media de toda su carrera profesional, (1.57 PPP). El entrenador nacido en Moreira de Cónegos, se formó en las categorías inferiores del Benfica, donde consiguió ganar una UEFA Youth League. En 2023, asumió las riendas del USL Dunkerque, en Ligue 2, equipo con el que peleó por el ascenso a la máxima categoría del fútbol francés. Sus grandes números no pasaron desapercibidos y el FC Nantes, de Ligue 1, lo fichó en junio de 2025. Sin embargo, sus malos números hicieron que su estadía en el equipo del Loira Atlántico solo durase cinco meses, un total de quince partidos oficiales.

articles.title: Western Michigan Called 'Undefeated Football Team' by Boise St. HC After Controversial Michigan Game
articles.summary: Boise State head coach Spencer Danielson apparently doesn't feel Michigan's controversial season-opening win should impact Western Michigan's record.
articles.body:
Boise State head coach Spencer Danielson apparently doesn't feel Michigan's controversial season-opening win should impact Western Michigan's record.

Danielson referred to Western Michigan as "undefeated" when discussing his team's upcoming matchup against the Broncos.

"I saw a little bit of what happened with the Michigan, Western Michigan game early on—when I went back and studied this, unbelievable," Danielson said during a Monday press conference.

"I mean, they're an undefeated football team. Period, end of story... you watch that game, they absolutely beat Michigan, at Michigan, and that's not hype. That's what happened."

Michigan secured a 13-12 victory over Western Michigan on Sept. 5 when Bryce Underwood threw a Hail Mary touchdown one play after the game clock appeared to expire on a heave out of bounds. One second was ultimately put back on the clock, which the NCAA later concluded was a mistake.

Despite a MAC appeal and an NCAA ruling that "the outcome of the game would have been different" had correct instant replay protocol been followed, the NCAA and the FBS Oversight Committee both stated they didn't have the authority to overturn the final result.

The College Football Playoff also announced it lacks ability to strip the win from Michigan, but noted in a statement factors other than overall records impact playoff odds.

Western Michigan has gone on to defeat Monmouth and Rice since the controversial loss to Michigan. The Broncos will now look to improve to 3-1 when Boise State comes to town Saturday for a 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff in Kalamazoo.

articles.title: Akron Fan Added to College Football 27 Dynasty Mode After Winning Viral Contest to Serve as OC
articles.summary: Martin Whims II's first opportunity as an offensive coordinator ended in a turnover, but he is getting another chance in the college football world.
articles.body:
Martin Whims II's first opportunity as an offensive coordinator ended in a turnover, but he is getting another chance in the college football world.

The virtual college football world, that is.

EA Sports revealed College Football 27 players can start a dynasty coaching career with Whims, who was Akron's guest offensive coordinator for its first possession of its home opener against Robert Morris this season.

Those who start a career with Whims have the immediate contract goals of beating rival Kent State, improving on last year's MAC record and winning at least 25 percent of conference games.

Whims won a promotion where a season-ticket holder was chosen to be the offensive coordinator for a possession and work alongside head coach Joe Moorhead. That possession ended in a Marcel Williams fumble, although Akron was enjoying success and driving into opposing territory prior to the turnover.

"We were moving the ball," Whims said, per Joe Reedy of the Associated Press. "The initial script that we developed was successful. So unfortunately ended with a fumble. I still think it was a success on the field, as far as the promotion goes and for the university."

For his part, Moorhead said Whims "did an unbelievable job. We spent probably an hour and a half going over the game plan, discussing the opening script. We were rolling on the third-and-short. We were lined in the wrong formation and got the penalty which put us behind the sticks and we still converted it. So don't put that on Marty, put that on me. I think that thing would've ended up in the end zone."

Fortunately for Akron, it still emerged with a 45-10 victory.

And now gamers can rewrite the script with EA Sports' latest development.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappe reveals he was 'close' to joining Liverpool in 2016
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe says his mum was a "big fan" of Jurgen Klopp and wanted her son to move to Merseyside.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappe has revealed how "close" he came to joining Liverpool in 2016, saying he went against the advice of his mother who "fell in love" with Anfield.

The France and Real Madrid striker said the Reds tried to sign him at 18, while he was playing for Monaco in Ligue 1.

Former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp said the club laid on a private jet and food for Mbappe and his family in an attempt to sign him, before he eventually joined Paris St-Germain.

Speaking to the Athletic, Mbappe said his mum was a "big fan" of Klopp and wanted her son to move to Merseyside.

"I was close to [joining] Liverpool. The favourite destination for my mum was Liverpool. She wanted me to go there," he said.

"I didn't listen because I wanted to play in my city, Paris. I didn't want to leave my country before I was someone.

"But yes, my mum was always saying, 'Liverpool - you're going to be there, playing at Anfield, it's going to be insane for you'."

Mbappe, now 27, said his mother went out to Liverpool for the "first step" of the negotiation.

"She went to the city, the stadium, she met the people. She was like, 'it's a wonderful club, everybody's so kind, it's a family club, a big club', said Mbappe.

"She went to Anfield and fell in love with it. She watched a few games alone, to feel the atmosphere, because she wanted to imagine me in this stadium."

Klopp, who spoke about the possible move on Magenta TV as a pundit at the 2026 World Cup, explained how a flight was taken from Blackpool to Nice in France, where "the entire Mbappe family boarded a private jet with five rooms or something".

"We really went all out. Then we flew around in a circle, talked with the family, ate good food," Klopp said.

He said they had not wanted to be seen having talks - but the meeting proved fruitless.

"We flew in a circle. It was fantastic. And then he went to Paris," Klopp added.

"But in the end, I took the decision to go to PSG because for me, born and raised in Paris, there was no better feeling than to show I could be a star in my hometown."

Mbappe later joined PSG on loan, in a deal including an option for the move to become permanent for 180m euros (£165.7m). He went on to spend seven years in Paris, becoming the club's record scorer before leaving for Real Madrid in 2024.

articles.title: Luis Binks eager to make mark for Scotland
articles.summary: From searching for pizza with Thierry Henry to leading a Danish Superliga side, Luis Binks has taken an unconventional route to the Scotland squad, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
Every footballer has a story, but not many are quite as trippy as the one Luis Binks tells while sitting among the palm trees of La Manga, Scotland's training headquarters for a few days this week.

At 25, the Brondby centre-half and captain is pushing hard for a Scotland debut against Slovenia on Saturday, a spot in the heart of Sebastien Pocognoli's defence having opened up since Grant Hanley and John Souttar were jettisoned once the Belgian took over from Steve Clarke.

Binks, with a grandparent from Dunbar, is among the eight uncapped players in the new manager's squad.

That's a lot of new faces and a lot of new stories.

Binks talks about the early weeks of his time at Montreal Impact in the MLS; February to March, 2020. He was 18 and recalls: "I'd been at Tottenham since I was very young, but I just wanted to go and play first-team football.

"That was my biggest thing, to not get caught up in the whole youth system. I feel that if you get caught in that, it's not real football. I wanted to test myself."

Which brought him to Montreal where his manager was the great Thierry Henry.

"I'd signed in February and then we went into Covid lockdown in March," Binks explains. "I hadn't yet found an apartment. I was in one hotel and Thierry was in another. The one I was in was then shut down.

"He was staying at the Ritz on his own. They wanted to move me to a hotel by the airport and I didn't want to go because there was nothing there. It felt like prison, almost. One day I get a call from him, saying: 'Do you want to move to where I am? You can go on the other floor'."

The Ritz-Carlton is a five-star retreat with 129 rooms. Henry and Binks were the only residents.

"I'd go for runs in the morning and he'd be sat in the reception on his own. When I'd get back from the run, he'd still be sat there. I'd spend a few hours with him, just trying to pick his brains.

"I remember one night I was sat in my room just playing PlayStation and he rings me and goes, 'do you want to get a pizza?'. There's me and him driving around Montreal looking for a pizza. It's a bit surreal, but that was how it was.

"I'm saying it now like it's just anybody, but there's a big aura around him. I was nervous at the time, but I asked him who's the best defender he's played with and against and why and it was a good time.

"It's a bit of a blur now, but I always remember him talking about Sol Campbell and just saying what made him great and how I could improve as a defender.

"I owe a lot to him because he gave me my first chance in senior football."

McPake's 'colourful' journey from club-less to Scotland call-up in three years

Scotland call for Montgomery as Tierney & McLean drop out

Binks is a highly regarded centre-half who's been around. Tottenham, then Montreal and then spells at Bologna (where he befriended Aaron Hickey), Como, Coventry and now Brondby.

The Scotland call-up just continues his upward trajectory.

"I woke up every day with it on the top of my mind," he says of this training camp ahead of a journey to Ljubljana for the Nations League opener on Saturday.

"It's pretty cool. It's a bit of a weird feeling you don't get with club football. I'm buzzing to be here."

In the summer of 2025, Binks joined Brondby. "I wasn't really scared of the unknown," he says. "It was a chance for me to go and play again, hopefully play in Europe, fight for titles, cups. I want to win things. That was my whole reasoning."

He's the captain now, a role that sits well with him given that he spent so many years at Tottenham captaining pretty much every age-grade side he played for.

"People would say they could see that in me," he continues. "I'd only been at Brondby a year, so to be rewarded with that [captaincy] is a good sign. There's a lot of responsibility that goes with it.

"With Scotland, having been called up, the next thing is to try and play. It's my first camp, my first time meeting everyone, but deep down I want to leave a mark on this team."

articles.title: Florentino también carga contra el periodista Juanma Castaño
articles.standfirst: Califica de "absolutamente deplorable e inadmisible" el paralelismo del periodista en un artículo publicado hoy en ABC y se reserva el derecho a emprender acciones
articles.summary: Califica de "absolutamente deplorable e inadmisible" el paralelismo del periodista en un artículo publicado hoy en ABC y se reserva el derecho a emprender acciones
articles.body: El Real Madrid emitió este martes un comunicado en el que censura con dureza las palabras del periodista Juanma Castaño, que en un artículo publicado hoy en el diario ABC comparó a Realmadrid TV con el diario Gara. El club considera la equiparación "absolutamente deplorable e inadmisible". En su columna, titulada 'El Real Madrid, en guerra', Castaño escribió que "en la tele oficial, que es el diario Gara del ultraflorentinismo, piden abandonar las competiciones nacionales". La entidad blanca entiende que comparar su medio oficial con un periódico "cuya historia está vinculada al mundo de la banda terrorista ETA constituye un ejercicio extremadamente grave que traspasa todos los límites". El comunicado defiende que Realmadrid TV "ejerce legítimamente su derecho a informar y a defender los intereses" del club, de sus socios y de sus aficionados, y lo describe como el medio de comunicación oficial de "un club con 124 años de historia que representa la sensibilidad y los valores de millones de aficionados en todo el mundo". El club cierra su nota advirtiendo de que "se reserva el derecho de adoptar las medidas que considere oportunas ante un ataque que es del todo inaceptable". El artículo de Castaño abordaba la reacción del madridismo tras el derbi disputado en el Metropolitano. En él, el periodista reconocía que "las dos acciones más polémicas del derbi son rojas claras" y admitía que el club "tiene todo el derecho del mundo a expresar su enfado con el árbitro, el VAR y el CTA", si bien sostenía que centrar en el arbitraje "los males de este club es ser un ciego ante algo que viene de muy atrás".

articles.title: Why Penn State football may be without Koby Howard vs Wisconsin
articles.summary: Penn State football could be without injured star receiver Koby Howard and tight end Andrew Rappleyea for its Big Ten opener on Saturday, Sept. 26.
articles.body:
Penn State football could be missing its most electric player for its Big Ten season-opener on Saturday, Sept. 26 .

Sophomore receiver Koby Howard − one of the nation's most productive receivers so far − suffered an undisclosed injury during his dynamic 70-yard, catch-and-run touchdown play in last weekend's 55-13 victory over Buffalo , coach Matt Campbell said during his weekly Tuesday press conference.

Howard "got dinged up" on the play and is now "questionable" for Saturday evening's game against Wisconsin in Beaver Stadium .

"Right now, we probably don't know exactly where he'll be by the end of the week. ... Just trying to gauge exactly where is he as we get ourselves ready for the end of the week," Campbell said.

Junior tight end Andrew Rappleyea also is "questionable" for Wisconsin after he suffered an apparent upper-body injury vs. Buffalo , Campbell said. Rappleyea left the field soon after catching an 18-yard touchdown pass in the game.

Meanwhile, the Nittany Lions , 3-0 and ranked 14th nationally , do expect to have starting center Brock Riker back after he missed most of the Buffalo game with an injury issue, Campbell said.

Howard exited against Buffalo early in the second half after making three catches for 115 yards and adding a 20-yard touchdown run. He's averaging an astounding 28.7 yards on his 12 receptions.

Howard is ranked seventh nationally in total receiving yards (344) and average per game (114.7).

Consider that the Lions' top three receivers last season (Devonte Ross, Trebor Pena, Kyron Hudson ) combined to average only 103 yards per game in 2025.

Check out our Penn State football vs Buffalo photo gallery: Best images

If Howard cannot play Saturday, the Lions figure to focus on senior wideout Chase Sowell , junior Brett Eskildsen and freshman Zay Robinson. The trio has combined for 22 catches and three scores through three games.

Unranked Wisconsin (2-1) is coming off blowout victories over Eastern Michigan and Western Illinois. The Badgers ' season began with a decisive defeat to Top 10 Notre Dame.

articles.title: Arteta, más cerca de Wenger: inminente renovación con el Arsenal
articles.standfirst: El técnico español termina su contrato en 2027 y seguirá con un contrato largo y mejorado
articles.summary: El técnico español termina su contrato en 2027 y seguirá con un contrato largo y mejorado
articles.body: El Arsenal anunciará próximamente la renovación del contrato de Mikel Arteta, el entrenador que les ha llevado a conseguir la Premier League pasada (tras 22 años de sequía), amén del subcampeonato de Europa. Mikel termina contrato el próximo verano (2027) y ha negociado un vínculo de larga duración (podría ser cinco años, hasta 2032), con condiciones mejoradas y, sobre todo, con la absoluta confianza de la propiedad, encarnada en Stan Kroenke, máximo accionista del club y uno de los hombres más ricos de Estados Unidos, con una fortuna de unos 21,3 mil millones de dólares, según Forbes. MA llegó al Arsenal en diciembre de 2019, y su última renovación fue en septiembre de 2024. Con este nuevo contrato, encamina ya la década en el club. Aludiendo al título de esta información, recordemos que el mito Arsène Wenger estuvo 22 años en el Arsenal, desde 1996 a 2018. La continuidad de Mikel será también la de su cuerpo técnico al completo, tan importante en los éxitos de un Mikel que, desde que está en Londres, ha conquistado la citada Premier, una FA Cup y tres Community Shields.
